verdict_reasoning: No reviewer disputes the goal, but the thread has already set aside the v1 design. In messages #5 to #7 the author agreed to drop three derivable counters and to build the exited-plus-live stats infrastructure first, yet the CF entry still holds v1 (maintenance-fit-1, standards-compat-2). v1 also loses the counters of exited backends (maintenance-fit-2). Code review makes sense once a version exists on the agreed design.

brief.title: Per-backend cumulative AIO counters via pg_stat_get_backend_aio()
brief.problem: Users cannot see how AIO ran over time. pg_aios shows only in-flight handles, and pg_stat_get_backend_io() counts IO volume, but not whether IOs ran sync or async, whether a backend waited for free handles, or which backends processed completions.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds cumulative AIO counters to the existing backend statistics kind (pgstat_backend.c), incremented from the AIO staging, completion and submit paths. pgstat_flush_backend() gets a new flag to flush the AIO counters. There is no global view, so stats of exited backends are lost.
user_visible_surface: New function pg_stat_get_backend_aio(integer) returning one record per PID.
Columns: started, executed_sync, executed_async, completed_self, completed_other, handle_waits, submitted, stats_reset.
No data for checkpointer, background writer, startup process and autovacuum launcher.
completed_other is documented as meaningful only with io_method = io_uring.
New flag value for pgstat_flush_backend() in the backend stats C API.
author_claims: The counters help tune AIO, for example handle_waits suggesting io_max_concurrency is too low.
The author observed no measurable regression; the cost is about 4 function calls and counter increments per IO.
Per-backend memory cost is 56 bytes for PgStat_AioCounters.
executed_sync and executed_async match the normal and bulkread read counts of pg_stat_get_backend_io() in his example.
No PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID bump is needed because backend stats are never written to disk.
brief.thread_state: Andres Freund questioned derivable counters, the lack of stats for exited backends, and pgstat_backend.c as a direction, proposing shared exited-backend plus live per-backend counters. The author agreed to do that redesign first in a new thread; the CF entry still holds v1, which a reviewer tested functionally.
unclear: No benchmark numbers or workload are given for the no-regression claim, at the hot AIO call sites.
No revised patch drops the derivable counters (started, executed_async, completed_self).
The material does not say whether this CF entry stays open while the redesign thread proceeds.
The proposal does not say how IO worker completions would be counted in worker mode.
No global view or reset function for these counters is defined.

objections.title: v1 grows pgstat_backend.c, a direction the thread already questioned
objections.failure_scenario: A committer applies v1 from the CommitFest entry, and the AIO counters become one more stats family inside the backend stats kind. Each later per-backend counter set lands in the same file with its own flush flag. The planned exited-plus-live redesign then has to move or rewrite all of them.
objections.argument: In message #5, Andres Freund doubts that pgstat_backend.c is the right direction because it will collect "all kinds of stats". He proposes per-kind shared counters for exited backends plus live per-backend counters. In message #7 the author agreed to do that redesign first in a new thread. The CF entry still holds v1, which uses the design both sides set aside.
objections.author_must_show: Should this CF entry be withdrawn until the exited-plus-live infrastructure exists, so that the AIO counters are built on it rather than on pgstat_backend.c?

critic.reasoning: Messages #5 and #7 confirm that both sides set aside the pgstat_backend.c design, and the CF entry still holds v1. A version built on the redesign would answer this, so the severity is fixable.

objections.title: v1 column set conflicts with the agreed redesign
objections.failure_scenario: v1 is committed from the open CF entry. Monitoring tools then query started, executed_async and completed_self. The redesign in message #7 drops these derivable columns and adds a total across exited backends, so those queries break or change meaning in the next release.
objections.argument: The author agreed in message #6 to remove started, executed_async and completed_self, and agreed in message #7 to land the redesign first. The CF entry still offers v1 as "Needs review". In [P6] a pg_stat_io extension was set aside so that the view's meaning would not change between releases, and the same reason applies to this function's contract. Exposing v1 now would set a column list that the thread has already rejected.
objections.author_must_show: Should this CF entry be withdrawn until a version exists with the reduced column set and an aggregate over exited backends?

critic.reasoning: The author agreed in message #6 to drop the derivable columns, but no revised patch exists and the CF entry still holds v1. P6 is only a loose parallel, and the objection stands without it.

objections.title: Completion columns change meaning with io_method, silently zero by default
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA on a server with io_method = worker, the default, reads completed_other = 0 and a small completed_self. The DBA concludes that completions are not shared or that IOs did not complete. The numbers never say that worker mode hides completions, so the DBA learns this only from a note in the docs.
objections.argument: The doc hunk calls completed_other meaningful only under io_uring, because IO workers do not track these statistics. Message #8 likely ran in worker mode, and it shows completed_self = 224 against executed_async = 26495. So completed_self also undercounts there, and the docs do not say so. Under the default setting the columns return plausible numbers with no sign that they are incomplete, and the meaning of the columns depends on a GUC.
objections.author_must_show: Under io_method = worker, what should completed_self and completed_other report, and why not return NULL or count completions on the worker side?

critic.reasoning: The doc hunk limits only completed_other to io_uring. Message #8 shows completed_self = 224 against executed_async = 26495, and the docs do not explain that gap.

objections.title: Per-IO counter calls on AIO hot paths have no published measurement
objections.failure_scenario: Every server pays four function calls and counter updates per IO in pgaio_io_stage(), pgaio_io_process_completion() and pgaio_submit_staged(), whether or not anyone reads the function. On a high-IOPS io_uring workload, a small regression would appear only after release, with no numbers to compare against.
objections.argument: Message #3 asks for a review of these call sites because they run for all workloads by default. Message #1 reports no measurable regression but gives no workload or numbers. Andres Freund in message #5 says the overhead "might be ok" but questions the number of counters per IO. If ten monitoring patches each add a few calls per IO, the AIO path slows for everyone.
objections.author_must_show: What does a high-IOPS benchmark of small random reads under io_uring and worker mode show, with and without the reduced counter set?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 asks about the cost at these call sites, and message #1 gives no workload or numbers. Andres Freund says the overhead "might be ok" and the pattern copies pgstat_count_backend_io_op(), so this is a request for numbers.

objections.title: Per-backend-only function fixes a user surface the redesign will change
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA monitors pg_stat_get_backend_aio() across parallel queries. The parallel workers exit, so their counters disappear, and the totals undercount AIO activity. If a global view arrives in a later release, the existing function and its columns must stay, or users' monitoring queries break.
objections.argument: The proposal has no global view, loses the stats of exited backends, and reports nothing for the checkpointer, bgwriter, startup process and autovacuum launcher. Andres Freund says in message #5 that stats for exited backends are almost always wanted. [P5] was reverted partly because its stats covered only some process types and not all users who needed them. Shipping the narrow function first commits the project to supporting it next to whatever the redesign produces.
objections.author_must_show: Can the function and its column set be defined so that they stay unchanged once exited-backend totals and a global view exist?

precedents.title: Revert "Track statistics for spilling of changes from ReorderBuffer".

critic.reasoning: Message #5 says stats for exited backends, such as parallel workers, are almost always wanted, and v1 loses them. The author's global view from message #6 is in no patch, and P5 records a comparable coverage gap.

refuted.title: No user demand shown beyond the author's own experiments
refuted.failure_scenario: Every installation pays about four extra calls per IO in pgaio_io_stage(), completion and submit. DBAs who never call pg_stat_get_backend_aio() still pay it. If few people use the counters, the project keeps a hot-path cost and a function signature that the planned redesign would replace.
refuted.argument: The only usage shown is the author's lab examples (messages #1, #2), one external blog post, and a functional test (message #8). No field report, -general thread or tuning case shows a user who could not diagnose AIO without these counters. In message #5 Andres doubts that most counters are useful, and three of the seven can be derived from others. Item 4 applies because the cost falls on all IO while the gain goes only to people who tune AIO.
refuted.author_must_show: Which real tuning cases, from users other than the author, needed handle_waits, executed_sync or completed_other, and what did those users do instead?

critic.reasoning: The per-IO cost part is a duplicate of maintenance-fit-3, and the derivable-counter part is a duplicate of standards-compat-2. The rest does not hold: pg_aios and pg_stat_get_backend_io() cannot report handle waits or sync fallback, and no reviewer disputed the goal.

precedents_retrieved.title: Get rid of pgstat_count_backend_io_op*() functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the pgstat_count_backend_io_op*() functions, so I/O counters are incremented once, and copies the pending I/O stats into the per-backend pending stats when the I/O stats flush. To make this work, per-backend stats must flush after the other stats kinds, first by placing PGSTAT_KIND_BACKEND last in the enum and later (v3) by flushing it outside the loop in pgstat_report_stat().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected to the ordering dependency between stats kinds at flush time, which so far have been independent, and said the copy approach hurts readability. He also said there was no benchmark data to choose among inlining, static structures, copies or fewer diffs, so the picture was incomplete. Andres Freund rejected the alternative WalUsage-style diff approach as too costly. The thread ends with the author disagreeing, and the visible messages do not show a final decision.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Hmm.  I really have an issue with the ordering dependency this
introduces between stats kinds, assumed to happen inside the code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve management of SLRU statistics collection.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Improve management of SLRU statistics collection.
Reverted commit(s): Move each SLRU's lwlocks to a separate tranche.; Collect statistics about SLRU caches
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Instead of re-identifying which statistics bucket to use for a given
SLRU on every counter increment, do it once during shmem initialization.
This saves a fair number of cycles, and there's no real cost because
we could not have a bucket assignment that varies over time or across
backends anyway.

Also, get rid of the ill-considered decision to let pgstat.c pry
directly into SLRU's shared state; it's cleaner just to have slru.c
pass the stats bucket number.

In consequence of these changes, there's no longer any need to store
an SLRU's LWLock tranche info in shared memory, so get rid of that,
making this a net reduction in shmem consumption.  (That partly
reverts fe702a7b3.)

This is basically code review for 28cac71bd, so I also cleaned up
some comments, removed a dangling extern declaration, fixed some
things that should be static and/or const, etc.

precedents_retrieved.title: WAL-logging facility for pgstats kinds
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a new "PgStat" resource manager and a pgstat_xlog_data() entry point so that any pgstats kind, including custom ones, can WAL-log its own stats data. Each kind handles replay through a redo callback in PgStat_KindInfo, so it can decide how the data persists on standbys and after crash recovery.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that stats only make sense on a replica or after a crash when they cover changes that are already WAL-logged, so they should be rebuilt during replay from the WAL records of the underlying objects. For table stats he proposed keying relation stats by relfilenode. He repeated the objection when the entry moved to the next CF, and the author then withdrew the patch and kept it aside.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I can't think of a real case where we would want to WAL log the stats
themselves, rather than re-emitting stats during replay based on the WAL
record of the "underlying object".

precedents_retrieved.title: s/shm_mq_iovec/struct iovec/
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace the shm_mq module's own shm_mq_iovec struct with the standard POSIX struct iovec. The motivation was to remove a duplicate definition now that struct iovec can be used everywhere.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas argued that the two structs belong to separate APIs and should stay separate. Reusing struct iovec could tie shm_mq to POSIX limits such as IOV_MAX, and it would stop shm_mq from adding its own fields later. The author accepted this and marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
They serve a similar purpose,
but they belong to completely separate APIs; I think "incidental
deduplication" is the right term for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

roaster_notes.note: The prior-attempt concern is coverage that P5's revert recorded: stats for exited backends and for IO workers. Andres raised it in message #5, and in message #7 the author chose to do the exited-plus-live redesign first, so the thread has settled it. The CF entry still holds v1 under Needs review, but the thread has replaced it. Without a new version, there is nothing new to object to from this angle.
The function name, the per-PID function form and the stats_reset column follow pg_stat_get_backend_io(). No new GUC, syntax or dumped object is added.

The proposal adds no persistent or cross-node state. Backend stats are never written to disk, so there is no stats file format change and nothing for pg_upgrade to handle. The catalog change is one new pg_proc entry with a catversion bump, which is routine for a major release. There is no WAL, replication or wire protocol change. The pgstat_flush_backend() flag and struct changes are internal and land only in a new major version, so ABI and backpatching are not affected.

The proposal has no real privilege or exposure aspect. pg_stat_get_backend_aio() exposes only per-PID IO counts, follows the same access pattern as the existing pg_stat_get_backend_io(), and adds no new privilege, escalation path, RLS bypass, or unbounded resource use an unprivileged user could drive. Not checked without the code: whether its permission checks match pg_stat_get_backend_io() exactly.

No existing feature, view or extension gives cumulative sync versus async execution, handle waits or cross-backend completion counts; pg_aios shows only in-flight handles and pg_stat_get_backend_io() counts volume by context. Two overlap points were raised and accepted in the thread: the derivable counters and the duplicate per-backend mechanism in pgstat_backend.c (messages #5 to #7).
One demand objection only. The redesign that the author agreed to in message #7 may change which counters exist, so demand should be judged again against that version.
